evidence: Added one test, test_prefix_a_popup_keys_only_walks_status_tabs_phase_sections_phase_detail_and_the_second_task, to tests/test_tmux_integration.py. It changes only that file and adds an `import time`. The test seeds its own phase "px-later" (planned, so it starts collapsed) with two tasks, px-first and px-second. It sends keys only through the existing tmux pty client.
Key sequence, with the rendered text asserted after each step:
- `1`, `2`, right, left, `1` switch tabs. The Running and Ready tabs filter the task rows.
- Up arrow three times puts the cursor on the phase header. Enter expands it, and px-first and px-second appear.
- `p` opens the phase detail ("planned · 0/2 tasks"). Esc returns to the list.
- `j` twice moves the cursor to the second task, px-second, which is below the first row. Enter opens the detail for px-second (shows "px-second tmuxfx"). The test asserts that "title of px-first" and the list rows are absent. Esc returns to the list.
- The test finishes with a check that only one tmux pane exists.
The test redraws via refresh-client and polls until the expected text appears and the unwanted text is gone.
Runs of the new test alone with `-k keys_only`: 6 of 6 passed, about 7.3 s each.
Full suite (`uv run --with textual --with pytest python -m pytest tests -q`): 301 passed, 0 failed, in 408 s.
Committed as 671220a, "test: walk tabs, phase sections and task detail by keys in the popup". Not pushed. The working tree is clean.
observations: In the popup, the cursor stays on the row index it had after a tab switch, so the cursor is not on the phase header after returning to the Active tab. The test presses up arrow three times first, which clamps at the top. The `j` presses show no visible change in the stripped text, so only the final Enter proves the cursor reached px-second. The phase detail loads asynchronously and briefly shows "Loading…".
